title: K-flat complexes remain K-flat under open restriction
statement: Let $j:X\to Y$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $K^\bullet$ be an unbounded cochain complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] which is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Termwise restriction by $\operatorname{Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor}(j)$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] gives a K-flat complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. No quasi-coherence or boundedness hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Cohomology, lemma-check-K-flat-stalks, applied to open restriction; Mathlib Scheme.Modules.restrictStalkNatIso

proof.text: Apply the forward implication of the stalk criterion to K on Y. Each stalk complex K_(j x) is K-flat.

The fully proved open-restriction stalk comparison identifies the restricted complex stalk at x with extension of scalars of K_(j x) along j.stalkMap x. Extension of scalars preserves K-flatness without any flatness hypothesis. Map this chain isomorphism through tensoring with the arbitrary acyclic stalk test complex F, and transport acyclicity along the resulting chain isomorphism.
Apply the reverse implication of the stalk criterion on X. The condition is vacuous when X has no points. No boundedness or quasi-coherence is used.

proof_origin.place: Stalk criterion; together with Tag 06Y1, extension of scalars preserving K-flatness, and Tag 0098, stalk of pullback. Open restriction comparison proved directly from Mathlib germ formulas by Q1.
